name: Peru coastal El Niño (extraordinary)
headline: Kelvin waves reaching South America keep warm water against the coast.

sources.title: ENFEN Comunicado Oficial N° 16-2026 (14 September 2026): Alerta de El Niño Costero
Latin Times: Peru's Pacific Ocean reaches record heat (7 October 2026), the source of the anchovy-season line only

sections.The setup: ENFEN Comunicado Oficial N° 16-2026 (14 September 2026) maintained the Coastal El Niño alert and said the event would continue until mid-autumn 2027, with the highest probability of extraordinary magnitude from September 2026 to January 2027; Communiqué N° 17-2026 (28 September) kept the alert and the extraordinary magnitude through January 2027. ENFEN's technical report of 25 September 2026: sea-surface temperature anomalies reached up to +7 °C near the coast in the last two weeks of September; the weekly OISST anomaly in the Niño 1+2 region was +4.7 °C; on 22 September the marine heatwave covered the whole 150 nautical-mile coastal strip between 4°S and 18.5°S, and 76.7% of it had anomalies above +4 °C.
sections.The trigger: Kelvin waves reaching South America keep warm water against the coast.
sections.What amplified it: according to Latin Times (7 October 2026), the first anchovy season of 2026 ended on 10 June with only about 25% of the 1.91 million tonne quota harvested (official figure not found); early heavy rain in Tumbes and Piura; heaviest rain expected Feb–Mar 2027.
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
